newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OSCE's Gonzalez urges "real democracy" in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: OSCE's Gonzalez urges "real democracy" in Serbia.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez on Friday urged Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic to seize the chance to install "real democracy" in the country and end the current unrest.

Gonzalez, back from a mission to Belgrade for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), was speaking at a news conference after issuing a report saying the Serbian opposition won elections annulled by Milosevic.

"There exists an extraordinary opportunity for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to solve this concrete problem, to initiate real democracy in the country, and to reintegrate itself into the international community," Gonzalez said.
This chance, he added, "must be seized by the authorities, by the opposition and the citizens of Yugoslavia."

Outgoing OSCE chairman and Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti told the news conference he had telephoned Milosevic to tell him of the Gonzalez mission's findings -- which included an implicit appeal for opposition election victories to be reinstated.

Cotti said he expected the Serbian leader to make his response known early next week. Danish Foreign Minister Niels Petersen, who takes over the OSCE presidency on January 1, said the body would hold a full Council meeting at the end of next week in Vienna to consider Milosevic's reply.
